subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is Patrick Star in <Picture 1>, and the character alone is what <Picture 1> supplies: a pink starfish with a soft pointed tip on top of the head; warm pink skin scattered with darker pink freckle spots across the chest, shoulders, back and arms; two thick rounded arms with blunt fingerless hands; thick black curved eyebrows; and two large oval white eyes with small black pupils set close together.
<Subject 2> is the kelp shake cup in <Picture 2>, and the cup alone is what <Picture 2> supplies: two rounded glass bulbs, an upper and a lower, joined by a straight cylindrical waist banded with a red label reading "KELP SHAKE"; the glass is filled with a glowing yellow-green shake that shifts from pale yellow at the top to grass green at the bottom, with small bubbles and bright star-shaped sparkles suspended inside it; a striped yellow-green lid caps the upper bulb and a striped yellow-green straw bends over at the top.
<Subject 3> is Patrick Star's house in <Picture 3>: a smooth dome of deep brick-red stone, wider than it is tall, sitting flat on pale speckled sand, topped by a single brass weather vane - an arrow pointing left with a crossbar tail - with a ragged fringe of dark green-brown moss running around the base of the dome. Around it, clear blue water-sky fills the space above the sand, scattered with flat flower-shaped clouds.
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 1> (S1).

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] The target video is a fifteen-second vertical handheld selfie in which <Subject 1> holds the camera up in one hand at arm's length and starts by shoving <Subject 2> right up against the front lens with the other, so that the opening frame holds nothing but the cup; the camera then pans horizontally off the cup to find him and locks there, settling on his face for a chest-up close-up in which he drinks and spits the mouthful out, drops the cup hand out of frame while the camera hand stays up, erupts into nine unbroken seconds of gibberish that end in three seconds of tongue-whipping, and finishes with a single bark. <Audio 1> supplies the voice timbre for <Subject 1>'s speech.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved from the moment the camera pans onto him - the soft pointed tip of the head, the darker pink freckle spots across the chest and arms, the thick black eyebrows, and the large oval eyes are retained to the end of the take.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the two glass bulbs, the banded label, the yellow-green shake with its bubbles and sparkles, the striped lid, and the bent striped straw are retained from the opening frame until the cup leaves the frame.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): small in the background from the moment the camera pans onto <Subject 1> onwards - the deep brick-red dome, the brass weather vane on top, the moss fringe at its base, the pale speckled sand, the blue water-sky, and the flat flower-shaped clouds.
<Audio 1>: reference - its timbre guides <Subject 1>'s speech without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a fifteen-second 2D hand-drawn cartoon in the style of the SpongeBob SquarePants animation, with bold dark outlines, flat color fills, and clean saturated color. It is shot on a handheld front-facing camera held in <Subject 1>'s own hand at arm's length, vertical 9:16, and apart from the single pan that brings him into frame that camera holds one fixed position and one fixed framing for the rest of the take. <Subject 1> performs with cartoon squash-and-stretch throughout: his jaw hinges far wider than a real mouth would allow, his face deforms well past anatomical limits and snaps back on every phrase.
[Shot 1] <Subject 1> holds the camera up in one hand at arm's length for the entire take and keeps it up in his hand the whole way through; the other hand, the one not holding the camera, holds <Subject 2>. The take opens with that front lens pressed right up against the cup: the frame is filled edge to edge by the kelp shake cup - its two rounded glass bulbs, its banded label and its bent striped straw - with only his blunt hand holding it visible along the edge of the picture, and <Subject 1> himself off frame. The cup knocks against the glass of the lens with a hollow thud, and Patrick Star (S1), speaking with the voice timbre referenced from <Audio 1> and his jaw dropped into a huge black oval cavity, shouts: <d>[English] Cheers!</d> As soon as the hit lands he pulls the cup away, and the camera pans across in one horizontal sweep at a steady speed to find him, swinging off the cup and onto his face, and from there the camera locks: it holds one fixed position and one fixed framing, giving a tight chest-up close-up in which the frame cuts across his ribs so that his head, shoulders and chest fill the whole picture, with <Subject 3> now small in the background behind him, at the natural wide-angle distortion of a front lens held close to the face. He tips his head back and pulls hard on the straw, one long drink, his head tipping back inside the frame as the shake drains down inside the glass bulbs; then he spits the mouthful straight back out in a wide yellow-green arc that sprays across the frame, his head whipping to one side with the effort. He then lets the cup hand fall loose and drop out of the bottom of the frame, taking the cup with it, while the camera hand stays up and the fixed framing holds exactly where it was, so that only his head and chest remain in the picture. He launches into a torrent of gibberish (S1) that runs for nine unbroken seconds - nonsense syllables fired out at speed with no recognizable word anywhere in them, rising in pitch and volume the whole way, his jaw falling open wider and wider, his eyes bulging into full white circles with tiny pinprick pupils, the pointed tip of his head flexing and bending with each burst, his chest tipping back and lurching forward inside the frame. Over the last three of those nine seconds the words give out altogether and he does nothing but whip his tongue about: the long red tongue, already hanging past his chin, lashes side to side in great sweeping strokes, the tip flying out past one cheek and then the other while his whole head swings left and right inside the frame with it, drops of spit flying off across the picture, and the pointed tip of his head whipping along with the shake. He finally throws his head back and lets out one single sharp bark - a short, low, dry "woof" with the exact attack and pitch of a real dog rather than a cartoon impression - his head tipping back and up inside the frame as he does it, and he holds that pose through the last frame. From that one pan onwards the camera holds its single locked position in his own hand and the frame stays level, so every part of the performance plays out inside a still picture, from the first frame to the last.

overall_soundscape:
The kelp shake cup knocks hard against the camera lens with a hollow plastic thud. One long wet slurp through the straw, then the mouthful sprays back out and hits the air and the sand in a scattered patter. A slow underwater current moves across the sand while small bubbles rise and pop in the distance, and the take ends on one single sharp bark followed immediately by silence.
